title: A Meal Only for the Set Apart

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Take the ram for the ordination and cook the meat in a sacred place. At the entrance to the tent of meeting, Aaron and his sons are to eat the meat of the ram and the bread that is in the basket. They are to eat these offerings by which atonement was made for their ordination and consecration. But no one else may eat them, because they are sacred." - Exodus 29:31-33 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Aaron and his sons eat the meat of the ram and the bread from the basket — a meal made from the very offering by which atonement was made for them. They did not merely watch the sacrifice; they took it into themselves. What was offered for them became food to sustain them.

This is a striking picture. Atonement was not only something done on their behalf at a distance. It was received, consumed, made part of them. The sacrifice sustained the very people it had covered.

Jesus used shocking language along these lines when He spoke of Himself as the bread of life, saying that whoever feeds on Him will live because of Him (John 6:51-57). He was not speaking of cannibalism but of a deep receiving — taking Christ into ourselves by faith so that He becomes our sustenance, not merely our transaction. And at the Lord's Supper we still take bread and cup, receiving what was given for us. Do not keep the cross at arm's length as a doctrine you affirm. Feed on Christ. Let Him be your daily nourishment.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
Is Christ a doctrine I affirm, or genuine daily nourishment for my soul?
How can I "feed" on Christ more deliberately this week?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord Jesus, You are not only my sacrifice but my sustenance. Teach me to feed on You daily by faith, drawing my strength and life from what You accomplished for me. Amen.
